## 0. The format in one paragraph

A real task is posed to the real product as a plain-language business outcome with a measurable target, a deadline, and a rule the founder cannot break. The product acknowledges, plans, and asks one question. The fleet works on screen; the founder is its hands. The first failure is shown, not cut. One correction loop. Then a receipt: the artifact, the before/after numbers, the attempt count, and the cost — followed by the honest ledger, including what still needs a human. Cold open is the finished receipt. Out is a hard cut. Everything that can be faked is instead receipted.

---

## 1. The Genspark format, decoded

**The core law:** every claim on screen carries a receipt, and the failure takes are kept in the cut. The $65 win is only believable because the $15,000 loss is on the same ledger.

## 2. The NOMOI channel format

Name the on-screen grammar **THE RUN**. Every episode is one run. Every run is filmable by one person with a phone and a Mac. Every product demo on the channel — Dain, Basin, BreatheAct, Cognitive Wellness, RevenueFloor — must be expressible in the four-beat formulation (§2.3) before it is shot. If a beat is missing, the demo is not ready.

### 2.1 Episode skeleton — target 11:30 (scalable to 8:00)

| Timecode | Beat | On screen | Who leads |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0:00–0:10 | **Cold open: the receipt** | Final artifact full-frame (chat export, ledger, drafted letter). One line of VO. | Fleet artifact |
| 0:10–0:35 | **Premise & rules card** | `TASK N: NAME`, measurable target, deadline, the rule ("I can approve. I can't edit."), counter 0/N | Founder A-cam |
| 0:35–0:55 | **Stakes** | Walking vlog. What failure actually costs him (a real thread, real money, a real deadline) | Founder vlog |
| 0:55–1:20 | **Fleet lineup** | Who's assigned: Ari (Simli face) + named lanes as terminal panes; harness on screen | Fleet |
| 1:20–2:20 | **THE ASK** | POV screen-record + live voice note to Dain in WhatsApp | Founder → Dain |
| 2:20–3:10 | **THE ACKNOWLEDGEMENT** | Dain's real reply full-frame: restatement, plan, price, one question. Ari reads it if voiced | Dain |
| 3:10–5:40 | **Work montage** | Screen records, logs, counter advancing; founder's hands as physical proxy; reaction insert every 20–30s | Fleet |
| 5:40–6:40 | **THE JAM** | First failure unfiltered + founder audit ("Show me why" + the log) | Fleet fails; founder audits |
| 6:40–8:10 | **THE REFINEMENT** | One correction loop as real messages; re-run | Founder ↔ Dain |
| 8:10–9:20 | **THE RECEIPT** | Artifact to lens; before/after numbers; attempt count ("ran 4×, 2 failed, both shown") | Fleet artifact + founder read |
| 9:20–10:20 | **THE LEDGER (rug-pull)** | Cost in AED, founder minutes, API spend, what still needs a human | Founder A-cam + spreadsheet |
| 10:20–11:10 | **Escalation button + next task tease** | The one autonomous act that surprised him (real, logged); next `TASK` card | Fleet |
| 11:10–11:20 | **Hard out** | One line. Cut to black. | Founder |

Cutdowns per episode: 1× 60–90s vertical (ASK→JAM→RECEIPT), 2× 30–45s verticals (the JAM; the LEDGER). Hook ≤2s, captions burned.

### 2.2 Founder's on-camera role and exact shot list

The founder is **the operator's boss who got demoted to intern**: he sets the task, then serves the run. Deadpan documentary tone — he is an organizational psychologist watching a hire he doesn't fully control. Never acts; audits.

| Beat | Shot | Framing / gear | What he says (script skeleton — final words his) | What he does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cold open | S0 | Over-shoulder of Mac, phone on tripod | "This ran. Everything after this is how." | Hands only. No face until 0:10. |
| Premise | A1 | Locked-off medium, desk, window key 45° | "One task. One day. If Dain drops a thread, that's a real client I have to call back." | Reads the rules card aloud; on-screen text mirrors him verbatim. |
| Stakes | V1 | Phone front-cam, walking (Corniche / street) | "My inbound runs through this number. Until 6pm it isn't mine." | One take, three beats max, no script. |
| Fleet lineup | S1 | Mac screen record + Ari Simli window | (silent, or) "Ari's on comms. Lanes on research, drafting, posting." | Points camera at the harness as-is. No set dressing. |
| THE ASK | S2 | POV phone screen record + voice note, mic visible | "Dain — inbox is yours till 6pm. Book what's bookable. Escalate anything from [name]. Don't promise refunds. Ask me before anything spends money." | Speaks to Dain like an operator briefing a hire. Never reads a "prompt." |
| THE ACK | S3 | WhatsApp reply full-frame; Ari (Simli) reads it | (founder silent) | Lets the product hold the frame alone for 10–20s. |
| Work montage | B-roll | Hands macro: approving sends, printing, paying; screen records interleaved | VO over montage, 1 line per 4–5s | Physical proxy only. Reaction insert (chin-on-hand) every 20–30s. |
| THE JAM | A2 | A1 + log full-frame cutaway | "That went to the wrong thread. Show me why." | Names the failure, no spin. Holds the log on screen ≥20s. |
| THE REFINEMENT | S4 | Split screen: founder / message thread | Voice note: "Shorter. No exclamation marks. Redo the last three." | Exactly one correction loop. Not two. |
| THE RECEIPT | A3 | Phone/printout to lens — the taste-test shot | "Forty-one threads. Median first reply 54 seconds. Mine is three hours. Two escalations — both right. It ran four times; two failed; you saw both." | Holds the artifact to the lens. Says the numbers slowly. |
| THE LEDGER | A4 | A1 + spreadsheet full-frame | "Run cost: AED 31. My time: 40 minutes. It refused two things. Good." | Reads every cost line. Includes his own hours. |
| Button + tease | S5 | Screen record of the surprise act | "It also did this. I didn't ask it to." | Shows the logged autonomous act. |
| Hard out | A5 | A1 | "This run is over." | Hard cut to black. No subscribe plea — that lives in description + pinned comment. |

**Where the fleet takes over (founder fully off-camera):** S1, S3, work-montage screen segments, S5. Minimum 45% of runtime is screen-record-first — this is what makes the format solo-sustainable.

**Inverted-hierarchy beat (once per episode, mandatory):** Dain assigns the founder one physical errand the run requires — buy a specific item, be at a place by a time, sign a thing. Founder complies on camera. This is the NOMOI version of "Finish the framing," it costs nothing, and it is true.

### 2.3 The formulation pattern — binding spec for every Dain and product demo

**ASK → ACKNOWLEDGEMENT → REFINEMENT → RECEIPT**

1. **ASK.** A plain-language business outcome with a measurable constraint and a deadline, posed by a human inside the product's native surface (WhatsApp for Dain). Formula: *"I need [outcome] by [time], under [constraint]. You handle [scope]. Ask me before [boundary]."* Never a feature tour. Never the word "prompt."
2. **ACKNOWLEDGEMENT.** The product restates the task in its own words, states its plan and its price (time / API cost), and asks **exactly one** clarifying question — or states one assumption it will proceed on. Comprehension, not compliance theater.
3. **REFINEMENT.** The first output is shown imperfect. The human corrects once, in the product's native channel. The product adjusts and re-runs. This loop is the trust-builder; the first failure is never cut.
4. **RECEIPT.** A verifiable artifact + before/after numbers + attempt count + cost. If a claim can't be receipted, it isn't made.

Genspark lineage, for the record: ASK = "earn $100 by end of day" / "close Tim's list"; ACK = "I can draft an email to them right now."; REFINEMENT = the dry-run failures and re-engineering; RECEIPT = Square POS + $65/$42 ledger. We keep the grammar and replace the staging with logs.

### 2.4 Recurring segments (channel identity)

- **The counter** — persistent top-left `N/M` in every episode, every run.
- **The ledger** — the rug-pull honesty beat; always includes AED cost + founder minutes + refusal list.
- **"What it refused to do"** — 20–30s segment; boundaries shown as features.
- **The meta-receipt** — the fleet cuts and posts this episode's own verticals via the TikTok posting API; the live post is shown on screen at the end. Disclosed on screen: "Cut by lanes. Approved and posted by a human tap."

## 4. First three episode briefs

Each is tied to a product outcome the fleet can **actually perform today**, on camera, with receipts. Rule for all three: *if a capability isn't shipped by shoot day, the episode is the build* — Genspark aired the 10-minute pour; we air ours.

### 4.1 EP001 — Dain Bot: "TASK 1: MY WHATSAPP, YOURS TILL 6PM"

- **Outcome (real):** Dain operates the founder's real inbound for one working day: triages threads, drafts replies, books one real calendar slot, escalates what it must not answer.
- **ASK (voice note):** "Dain — inbox is yours till 6pm. Book what's bookable, escalate anything from [named thread], don't promise refunds, ask me before anything spends money."
- **ACK:** Dain's triage plan + one question, full-frame.
- **JAM (expected, welcome it):** a misclassified thread or an over-formal reply. Founder: "Show me why" → log on screen ≥20s.
- **REFINEMENT:** one corrective voice note (tone/length), re-run on the last three drafts.
- **RECEIPT:** chat export (redacted) + calendar entry + numbers: threads handled, median first-response time vs. founder's stated baseline, escalations count, attempt count.
- **LEDGER:** API cost in AED, founder minutes, and the refusal list ("it declined to promise a refund — good").
- **Anti-fabrication:** correspondents are real and consent on camera (5s voice note), or the counterparty is the founder's second device, **labeled on screen: "DEMO LINE — the customer is me."** No invented clients.
- **Verticals:** the JAM / the 54-seconds-vs-3-hours receipt / the one question.

### 4.2 EP002 — Basin: "TASK 7: EVERY DIRHAM, 7 DAYS"

- **Outcome (real):** every transaction the founder actually makes for 7 days is captured and categorized in Basin on his Android; week ends with an audited export.
- **Genspark mirror:** persistent `DAY n/7` counter + running spend ledger; cash spends as the physical beats (POS b-roll); the rug-pull is the miscategorization list.
- **ASK:** "Every dirham, filed, for 7 days. If you're guessing a category, flag it, don't file it."
- **JAM:** a missed capture or a wrong category — shown, not fixed off-camera.
- **REFINEMENT:** one rule correction via the lane; re-run on the week's flags.
- **RECEIPT:** Basin screens + exported CSV + accuracy audit on camera: e.g., "43 of 51 right; 8 fixed by hand — here they are" + time vs. his real old method (baseline stated in the premise beat, before the run).
- **Anti-fabrication:** real spends only, amounts unrounded; whatever capture method Basin actually ships is what's filmed — if entry is manual today, manual entry is the shot.
- **Founder shots:** POS POV, Friday ledger read (A4), the correction voice note.

### 4.3 EP003 — RevenueFloor: "TASK 12: FIND THE CLAUSE"

- **Outcome (real):** the fleet ingests real, public KSA payer/NPHIES/CHI documents and produces a checkable artifact: a denial-reason → policy-clause map, plus one appeal letter drafted against a quoted clause — verified on camera against the source PDF.
- **Data floor:** consented, de-identified denial data only if a real counterparty signs a consent card on screen; otherwise claim lines are synthetic and **labeled full-frame: "SYNTHETIC DEMO DATA."** The policy documents and the clause mapping are real either way.
- **ASK:** "This denial class keeps getting paid late. Find the clause that kills it. Cite it."
- **JAM:** a citation that doesn't survive the check — founder audits one clause by hand on camera (the trust beat; he is the referee).
- **RECEIPT:** source PDF with highlighted clause beside the drafted letter; numbers: docs read, clauses mapped, letter drafted in N minutes, API cost.
- **LEDGER:** what still needs a human (sign-off, submission, clinical coding judgment) — said out loud. KSA PDPL noted on screen.
- **Why this episode exists:** it's Genspark's sourcing-montage + receipts grammar applied to documents — no physical build required, and it proves RevenueFloor's core claim with public sources.


## 5. The floor — non-negotiables

### 5.1 No fabricated results

- Only runs that ran. Raw logs and screen records live in `/receipts/EP###/` before the edit locks.

## 6. Adversarial: what will NOT transfer, and what replaces it

| Genspark element | Why it fails for a solo founder | NOMOI replacement |
|---|---|---|
| **Crew + multi-cam** (camera op at 97s, EasyRig at 829.58s, studio two-shots) | He is one person with a phone. | Locked-off tripod A-cam + screen-record-first grammar (≥45% of runtime is screen). Movement comes from cutting, not operators. The "interview two-shot" becomes founder interviewing Ari via Simli — a real product surface, and a genuinely novel beat. |

## 7. Pre-flight checklist (tape to the tripod)

1. Premise card states target, deadline, constraint, baseline — before the run.
2. ASK recorded as a real voice note in the product's native surface.
